Subject: Per-token rebate inquiry and security gating

Hi Rishi / Neha,

Thanks for the demo last week — the tech looked solid and our LLM product team is excited. Before we get to a committed usage tier discussion, procurement has a hard requirement: we need the executed DPA and recent SOC 2 Type II evidence before we can sign contracts that include committed pricing/discounts.

Two quick questions:
- Is Redwood able to provide a redacted SOC 2 report or an interim attestation we can share with legal?
- If SOC 2 / DPA must be in place first, do you have an acceptable pattern for a temporary rate (or credit) during onboarding?

Appreciate a short checklist so we can move the deal forward.

Best,
Sarah
Sarah Lee
Senior Procurement Manager, Acme Retail
[sarah.lee@acme-retail.com]

Date: Sat, 2 May 2026 11:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Per-token rebate inquiry and security gating

Hi Sarah — thanks for the clarity. We can absolutely accommodate the SOC2/DPA requirement; below is a pragmatic path that has worked for other mid-market customers and keeps momentum:

Proposed phased approach (high level):
1) Sign commercial agreement + DPA via DocuSign to lock in baseline terms. We can circulate a standard DPA today. (link below)
2) Placeholder onboarding rate: we offer a 5% onboarding credit applied to the first 60 days of usage after signing.
3) Full committed per-token rebate (tiered by monthly token volume) becomes retroactive and unlocked once we receive either: (a) redacted SOC2 Type II report OR (b) a SOC2 bridge letter from your auditor, and the executed DPA, within 30 days of signing.
4) If evidence is not received in 30 days, we revert to the baseline rate; we can also apply a one-time temporary credit (negotiable) if you can provide a signed schedule agreeing to provide evidence within 45 days.

I've attached a draft SOW and a pricing term sheet showing the per-token tiers and example math. Action items:
- Please confirm the security contact (name + email) at Acme who will coordinate the SOC2 evidence.
- If legal needs a redline, loop in Ian and we can accelerate.

Attachments: draft_SOW.pdf, Redwood-pricing-term-sheet.xlsx
DocuSign (DPA): https://www.docusign.net/some-docu-sign-link/ABC123
HubSpot: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/123456/company/ACME-7890

If that plan looks sensible, I can prepare a short mutual action plan and have legal queue the DPA for signature.

Thanks,
Rishi Malhotra

Thanks — quick clarifications from procurement/legal:
- Our policy is to have SOC2 evidence on file before committing to preferred pricing. We can consider limited exceptions, but they require an internal escalation.
- We can provide either a redacted SOC2 report OR a SOC2 bridge letter signed by our auditor. Redacted reports are preferred.
- As an alternative to retroactive rebates, procurement asked whether Redwood would consider an escrow/holdback mechanism: i.e., Redwood invoices at list rate, Acme retains 10% of committed discount in escrow for 45 days and releases on proof of SOC2/DPA.

Please circulate the redacted SOC2 sample and any legal language you'd expect for an escrow/holdback. We'll route to our legal and IT security.

Regards,
Sarah

Hi Sarah — quick note from the commercial ops side with an alternate workable pattern:

Option A (preferred):
- Execute DPA + commercial agreement. Apply full committed tiered rebate retroactively once SOC2 / DPA delivered within 30 days.

Option B (if SOC2 must precede signature):
- Sign agreement with a conditional pricing schedule: Redwood provides a temporary credit pool equal to 7.5% of expected first-quarter usage (applied as monthly credits). Once SOC2 evidence is received, credits are replaced by the agreed per-token rebate and any under/over-crediting is reconciled.

Option C (procurement escrow):
- We can accept an escrow letter; legal will need a simple release condition: delivery of redacted SOC2 report to Redwood's security inbox (security@redwood.ai) within 45 days. We'll circulate a one-paragraph escrow release clause for legal review.

I'll open HubSpot case and attach a template clause we use for escrow releases. HubSpot ticket: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/123456/ticket/HS-8421

—Neha
